historical_external_evidence.interpretation: Historical external weak-label evidence only; not recomputed by this run and not local accuracy.
limitations: The experiment is proposal-only and does not change the trusted production prediction policy.
The empirical scope is limited to honeypot-observable Cowrie SSH/Telnet tactics, not full ATT&CK-wide tactic prediction.
The external seed labels inherit the quality and bias of the upstream classification pipeline; they are not manually adjudicated ground truth.

Only scorers computable from the external Cowrie session payloads are fitted. Context/risk scorers that require live enrichment, vulnerability context, Sigma correlation, or behavior-regime state are excluded from the fitted voter set.
Most external Cowrie sessions contain no tactic transition after scoping, so the held-out evaluation is based on the subset with usable next-tactic labels.
The held-out split is used only for final evaluation; production adoption of fitted weights should still be reviewed against local live honeypot data when enough high-quality labeled sessions exist.
No production improvement is claimed unless a supplied held-out set supports it.
The public package may include privacy-minimized external tactic sequences, but no raw Cowrie telemetry or local production sessions.
The retained external aggregate model is derived from an SSH/Telnet dataset and cannot alone establish SSH-only performance.
External tactic labels are classifier-derived weak labels, not independent expert ground truth.
Local prediction accuracy remains unclaimed when clean held-out local transitions are insufficient.
Returned scores are not called calibrated probabilities without held-out calibration evidence.

metric_semantics.brier_score: multiclass Brier score over a normalized returned probability vector; lower is better
metric_semantics.coverage: fraction of held-out cases receiving a non-empty ranking
metric_semantics.selective_top1_accuracy: Top-1 accuracy among covered cases only
metric_semantics.top1_accuracy: all-case accuracy; abstentions count as failures
metric_semantics.top3_accuracy_secondary: secondary because the external empirical scope contains few tactics

not_recommended_models.reason: The trusted tactics are already observed states and targets; latent-state semantics are not established.
Flattened tabular features add overfitting risk without a useful sequential inductive bias.
The retained evidence has only 854 transition-bearing external sessions and weak labels.
There is no defensible action, reward, or intervention-learning problem in this advisory predictor.
Exact next-command prediction is outside the Cowrie next-tactic thesis scope.

optional_dependency_status.multinomial_logistic_regression: skipped unless scikit-learn is supplied by the evaluation environment

scope_statement: Next observed MITRE ATT&CK tactic from trusted Cowrie honeypot-observable tactic sequences. The external comparison corpus is SSH/Telnet mixed or protocol-unknown and is not evidence of SSH-only accuracy.

thesis_defense_qa.answer: The target is the next observed tactic in a short trusted sequence, and the available evidence consists directly of interpretable transition counts.
thesis_defense_qa.question: Why use Markov-family models?

thesis_defense_qa.answer: Only 854 external sessions contain transitions and their labels are classifier-derived; that is insufficient for a defensible high-capacity neural sequence model.
thesis_defense_qa.question: Why not LSTM/Transformer?

thesis_defense_qa.answer: HMMs are useful when meaningful states are hidden. Here ATT&CK tactic candidates are already the observed states and prediction target.
thesis_defense_qa.question: Why not HMM?

thesis_defense_qa.answer: They would flatten the sequence into tabular features, add overfitting risk, and provide no demonstrated advantage over transition counts.
thesis_defense_qa.question: Why not Random Forest/XGBoost?

thesis_defense_qa.answer: It tests whether any sequential model improves on class prevalence and exposes inflation caused by tactic imbalance.
thesis_defense_qa.question: Why compare with Majority Class Classifier?

thesis_defense_qa.answer: It is the simplest well-known sequential baseline and isolates the value of longer context and cross-source adaptation.
thesis_defense_qa.question: Why compare with First-order Markov Chain?

thesis_defense_qa.answer: It is the incumbent runtime behavior, so it is the required reference for any improvement claim.
thesis_defense_qa.question: Why compare with the current hard-backoff model?

thesis_defense_qa.answer: Hard backoff chooses one source. The proposed model can combine external prior counts and validated local evidence continuously in one posterior distribution. In this external-only run no clean local update is available, so it reduces to a Dirichlet-smoothed external prior and does not demonstrate an improvement over hard backoff.
thesis_defense_qa.question: What differs between hard backoff and Empirical-Bayes smoothing?

thesis_defense_qa.answer: It supplies cold-start transition evidence when deployment-local trusted transitions are sparse.
thesis_defense_qa.question: How does the external Cowrie dataset help?

thesis_defense_qa.answer: The public package retains no local session corpus and documents only one clean local held-out transition.
thesis_defense_qa.question: Why is local accuracy not claimed?

thesis_defense_qa.answer: The shared trust predicate excludes audit-only, low-confidence, unsupported, and shell-noise classifications before sequence construction.
thesis_defense_qa.question: How are weak labels handled?

thesis_defense_qa.answer: The recorded 70/15/15 whole-session split is applied before transition cases are extracted, so no session crosses partitions. The external split is deterministic and stratified by first tactic transition, not chronological, because the retained source payload has no timestamps.
thesis_defense_qa.question: How is leakage prevented?

thesis_defense_qa.answer: The retained external model contains only six empirical target tactics, so Top-3 is comparatively easy and less discriminating than Top-1, MRR, and Brier.
thesis_defense_qa.question: Why is Top-3 secondary?

thesis_defense_qa.answer: The model emits no empirical next-tactic ranking when the observed context lacks the configured raw transition support.
thesis_defense_qa.question: What does abstention mean?

thesis_defense_qa.answer: Not automatically. They are normalized model scores unless calibration is fitted and evaluated on held-out data.
thesis_defense_qa.question: Are the scores calibrated probabilities?

thesis_defense_qa.answer: Results are limited to trusted Cowrie-observable evidence; external labels are weak labels, the retained corpus mixes SSH/Telnet, and local generalization is not yet estimable.
thesis_defense_qa.question: What limitation belongs in the thesis?
